To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the typing rules for the SML-Nj type system, in a form other that the source code, have been presented and proved correct; (2) the typing rules are sound with respect to a small-step operational semantics; (3) an application rule is formulated that is more general in allowing imperative arguments to be used in the application of a polymorphic function; and (4) the type rules for this rule are also presented and proved correct.

the SML-Nj compiler implements a type system that subsumes the system presented here, that the type system presented here is correct, and that the type system of SML-NJ can be implemented using a type system of only a slightly larger generality.

the design and implementation of a language and compiler for a class of imperative programs that use polymorphic functions.
the development of type systems for polymorphic imperative programs and the proof of soundness.
